title: Line Share Held After a Cured Property Charge Default: HECM Modified Plan Designations
content:
**Note.** Added to the amounts kept when the designated amount of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) loan is set, after a cured property charge default, is a share of the available line. The facts come from the loan's Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases records: the most recently cured maturity case is the case named by the loan's most recent cure confirmation notice.

| Most recently cured case | Cure confirmation notices sent on the loan after the same day of the month 36 calendar months before the handling date | Share held |
|---|---|---|
| a Property Charge Default closed as cured on a date after the same day of the month 12 calendar months before the handling date | two or more | 25 percent of the available line |
| the same | fewer than two | 10 percent of the available line |
| any other case type, a case cured outside that twelve-month window, or no cured case | any | nothing |

*Hypothetical cases (available line 50000.00, handling date 1 June):* a Property Charge Default cured on 15 March with two cure confirmation notices in the last 36 months holds 12500.00; with one notice, 5000.00; the same default cured on 1 June of the previous year holds nothing, as does a cured Sale or Title Transfer case.
